findings.title: The sync token schema strips required token fields
findings.body: These computed keys are not wildcards: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the same literal key for both entries, so the second property overwrites the first. Zod also strips unrecognized object properties by default. In credential-sync mode, parsing therefore drops fields such as `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, and `refresh_token`; token refresh then stores stale or missing values, causing repeated refreshes or unusable credentials.

findings.title: Persist the parsed credential, not the Zod result wrapper
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the entire `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this code stores that object as the credential key. After the first token refresh, the database key no longer has Google token fields, so subsequent authentication fails when it parses the credential or tries to refresh again. Store the parsed `data` instead.

findings.title: The synced refresh response is treated as a HubSpot token object
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw Fetch `Response`, but this code treats its result as `HubspotToken`. The response has no `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, or `expiresIn` properties, so the code computes and persists undefined token fields and sets an invalid HubSpot access token. Parse the response body into the expected token shape before using it.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint
findings.body: This refresh flow calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`, unlike the other integrations changed for this feature. With credential sharing enabled, Salesforce credentials therefore continue to refresh against Cal.com's configured app rather than the self-hoster's credential source of truth, so the advertised synchronization does not work for Salesforce.
